en: A Single-Practice Composition and Translation of the Secret Rite for the Ten Thousand Loves of Mañjuśrī-Yamāntaka,
the Wish-Fulfilling Dharma.
Now, as for the source of the Mantra teachings,
nothing is superior to the homa rite;
herein lies the secret teaching of the dharma of love.
In order to inspire reverence and affection among sentient beings in the final age,
I shall now proclaim a single-seal mantra,
for it is capable of benefiting all living beings.
First, the image is described:
its body has six faces, six arms, and six feet,
and it rides upon a water buffalo.
Regarding what are called the six faces:
the three faces on the crown—the central face—have the form of a Bodhisattva and are supple.
Upon the crown of that face is Amitābha Buddha.
Furthermore, he has six arms:
specifically, the left hands hold (1) a spear, (2) a wheel, and (3) a noose;
the right hands hold (1) a sword, (2) a precious staff, and (3) an arrow.
This is because it takes the form of that bow’s casting power.
Furthermore, there are six feet;
on the left, three feet stand upon wheels.
On top of these three feet is that wheel, beneath which is a wooden ox;
the ox stands on four legs upon a flower pedestal,
and behind its back there is a flame.
It is like a rainbow,
and also like vaidūrya.
Within that fire, there is an image of the deity Yin beneath his right foot.
Next are the twelve deities, though they have not yet been presented face-to-face.
Furthermore, regarding the water mandala and the circular mandala:
within that mandala, one may practice by placing a wheel.
The rites of increasing prosperity, winning affection, pacifying calamities,
and subjugating may all be performed;
furthermore, these oral transmissions must also be transmitted through both body and speech.
Furthermore, the oral transmission of the Single Seal is taught.
The mantra is:
Oṃ stīrikālarūpa hūṃ khaṃ svāhā. With this seal and mantra, one faces the Buddha.
Having accomplished the universal prostration and the sequential visualization,
he further explains the mandala ritual.
Within the inner court is the Vidyārāja.
On the back of the Vidyārāja is the Dharma-form Mañjuśrī.
In the eastern section of the outer enclosure is the Youth of Summoning;
his form is like that of a youth.
On top of his topknot is a crescent moon; he holds a bow and arrow.
In the southeast is the youth Kiśavani, with the same physical form as above;
his left fist and right hand grasp a three-pointed spear.
With the left fist placed at the waist,
the youth Jñānottara of the south has the same form as above,
with a wheel cast in his left hand.
On the right foot, bestowing fearlessness,
is the youth Upakeśinī in the southwest, with the same form as above,
holding two flower bowls in his two hands.
In the west is the youth Prabhārajāla;
his left fist rests at his waist,
and his right hand holds a peacock’s tail feather.
In the northwest is the youth Bhūmimati;
his right hand holds a trident,
like Vajragarbharāja.
In the north is the youth Vimalaprabha, with the same form as above;
his left fist rests at his waist,
and his right hand holds a noose aloft.
In the northeast is the Youth of Inconceivability (*Acintya-kumāra*).
His left fist rests at his waist,
and his right hand holds a sword on the ground in a striking posture.
Each body has five-colored wheels standing upright;
beneath each wheel is a lion.
He preached the Dharma in this manner.
He accomplished the preaching of the Dharma.
At the summit of a high mountain,
he constructed a pure chamber and remained silent for forty-nine days.
Extinguish the fire according to the ritual.
Once one million recitations are completed,
the accomplishment of the rite will be attained.
Furthermore, the dharmas that accomplish the seals are now explained.
Having thus explained the earth seal and the heaven seal:
Sentient beings of the末世 (matsujin) shall believe, accept, and practice this.
One fascicle of the *Yamadeka Man’aihō* (The Dharma of Ten Thousand Affections of Yamadeka).
Completed by one proofreading on the twenty-third day of the seventh month in the second year of the Hōgen era, at the residence of Saimei-in in the West of Kanshu-ji Temple.
The Monk Zhikai
